From June 9 - June 24, Steam is hosting the Season of Pride event presented by MidBoss which features over 50 LGBTQ+ inclusive games at up to 80% off, along with a bevy of special streaming engagements. 

In addition, all through July, seasonofpride.tv will be featuring a special Twitch schedule highlighting a fantastic collection of inclusive games played by amazing members of the LGBTQ+ streamers and raising money for The Trevor Project, Trans Lifeline, and GaymerX. The World's Smallest Pride Parade
In celebration of Pride and the LGBTQ+ community, a special event has been added to the game. While exploring the main street of Gator Bay, players can come across a group waiting to see the town's official (albeit tiny) Pride parade. This burgeoning parade is very small, but it represents a phenomenal shift in the town's attitude and politics toward the LGBTQ+ communities.

Players can converse with returning character(s) Morgan/Morrigan from Always Sometimes Monsters and either come to reconciliation, awareness, or comprehension of the change since their transition after first meeting them in Beaton. The parade itself is a short, but joyous spectacle, and should not be missed.

This content is timelocked and can only be accessed while playing in June.

notes.title: Starlust & Startups - Build Update #470

Aaaannndd.... we're back!

It's been a little while since we've written one of these update notices, but rest assured this is a good one. While we've been off releasing The Stonks Market, releasing Always Sometimes Monsters on Nintendo Switch, and prepping our studio for the next big project, we've been slowly adding small improvements and new content to Sometimes Always Monsters.

While, as mentioned, the studio is getting ready to step into production on its next major production, we remain commited and eager to continue improving SAM and adding new content to the game. More new updates will continue to come in future months, though more periodically than they have previously been. 

Stay tuned to the Vagabond Dog Twitch Channel for day-to-day developments, join the Discord Server to request content, and stay tuned here to see all the latest updates.


Desdemona's Starlust
On the beaches of Gator Bay, you catch the eye of an attractive young woman. She takes interest in you and one thing leading to another can lead to another and again. It's wise to keep your wits about you though, as eager hearts are often too hasty and intentions can be very hard to read.

Also, you're still married. ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)

Quickstarter
The Quickstarter co-op working space is now open for business in Slab Town. The shared office is available to players for $80 per day and provides a comfortable desk outside of the bus where they can finish their book. Such a comfortable work environment is sure to boost your productivity. In addition, there's a variety of included ameneties.

Inside the office, you'll find two young game developers with some anxiety issues about their projects. They're in a competition of sorts, and you may be asked to provide advice, or take a role spying for one.

Additional New NPCs
Some additional characters have appeared in Slab Town, including a rather bizarre individual named Fenrir who seems to have hit his head rather hard, and a writer named Serge who is suffering from some depth of writer's block. Upon encountering either of these individuals, you can help their predicament to some degree with a friendly conversation. Serge can be found in the coffee shop, and Fenrir can be found pacing around the main square.

Karen's Friend, Joyce
Karen's meek but beloved friend, Joyce has made an appearence at the CellBlock Mobile shop in Gator Bay. She's been there a really long time, waiting for a technician to help her with her phone. It doesn't seem to work after she clicked a link for a free cruise.

Happy Halloween, everyone!
We've got a very special update for those of you who want a little extra spooky with your Monsters.

In addition to some fun content that's only available if you play the game on Halloween (or change your system time to match), the entire series is also on sale for the weekend. You can catch both Sometimes Always Monsters and Always Sometimes Monsters as part of Steam's Halloween Spooktacular.

Halloween Pranksters
Players who are in their home, either by reaching the epilogue or never going on the tour, can enjoy a fun Halloween experience if they play the game on October 31st.

Speaking to your spouse while your computer's clock reads 10/31 will have them recognize the holiday and give you some special candies before they head out to visit a friend. If you're divorced in your epilogue, you'll have a special phone call fulfilling the same purpose.

In the evening on this day, you'll be visited by a string of children who've come for trick-or-treating and expect to be given candy. We've expanded the Music app on the player's phone to now display album artwork, song titles, and the band name through an overlay across the top portion of the screen. This comes alongside a renovation to the application that will allow us to continue expanding the musical selection hereafter.

NPC Cameo: Napostriouf
There's a new character on the beach of Gator Bay. He's chilling on the far east side, having a little picnic with some random street cats that have taken to his company. Be wary though, as engaging as his lengthy (partially French) conversation may be, there's definitely something off about him and his cats.

notes.title: Fake Saves & Soap Suds - Build Update #458
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/24174678/77685af3a6ab3cbbe86118902ca826f6b23f84ce.png

We've had a pretty busy month since the last update...

In addition to building and releasing Karen: An Outrage Simulator, we've been cooking up some new content for Dog Gone Golfing, and delivering high-quality development streams almost every day on our Twitch Channel.

Atop all that, we've not forgotten our commitment to continually improving the Sometimes Always Monsters, and have thus prepared another juicy update since the release of the Author Outfit DLC Pack.

Although we're only working about 3 days per week on new SAM  content as we expand into new projects, we'll be keeping a maintainable schedule as the months roll on. Our hope is to keep adding new free content for all of you to enjoy, as long as we can manage it on the calendars. We truly love this game, and appreciate the amazing reception to these regular updates.

Save Faker
Long requested (even before the release), we've finally created a system by which players can fake their Always Sometimes Monsters save files if they're unable to locate their originals. This will be a big help to anyone whose file wasn't stored in the Steam cloud, or for anyone who first played ASM on mobile or PlayStation.

The process begins when you select New Game, and involves a short, spoiler-filled questionaire about your experience in ASM. From that, it'll make a new save state with an approximate replication of your prior reality. Please be mindful that because it is an approximation of your save and the whole data does not persist, several elements may not be exact.

While we may still change how and where the questionairre is presented, we hope those of you who've been waiting for this feature now have the entry point you desire. As an added bonus, those of you who've already played Sometimes Always Monsters can now more easily replay the game with a new variation on the entrance continuity.

NPC Cameo: Karen
Thanks to a reward redeemed on our Twitch Channel, we've included another small NPC cameo. Though, this time it's not for the lead of our brand new game, Karen: An Outrage Simulator.

You can find Karen in the New Creole book store, where she is discussing the return policy in regards to a particular book she'd like exchanged. Be careful how you approach, as once she gets fired up, she'll blow right past you and any companion you've brought along.

Indie Heroz
Another feature returning from ASM is the ability to find and collect a series of figurines that feature characters from other great indie games. On your next playthrough, you'll be able to scour the cities for a bunch of hidden collectibles that'll show up in their own category within your inventory. See how many you can find, and how many of their games you can recognize!

Lockdown Ends
After 6 long months of being shut to the public, the Vagabond Dog office in Slab Town is finally reopened. You can pop into the space, see what the developers are up to, explore their workspace, and get opinions from any companion you bring in there.

Please be mindful not to bother the team too much. They're hard at work on their latest projects.

NPC Cameo: Concert Photographer
Another reward redeemed through the Twitch Channel has added a new character to the Gator Bay club scene. You'll be able to meet a concert photographer named Carles who'll talk to you about Darkeff or Viper, get your opinion on music, and possibly take your photo. 

Soap Suds
Do you hate nudity? Would you prefer a more coy shower experience? Well, now when you use soap while washing there will be some tastefully placed bubbles to occlude the the view of your naughty bits.

It's a dumb feature that pretty much nobody asked for, but whatever. It's in the game now.

Don't forget you can always see what we're working on via the Twitch Channel, where we broadcast our development almost every day from 1PM - 5PM EST.

If it's been a little while since your first time through Sometimes Always Monsters, we've got a hot new update that's makes it a great time to re-enter for another tour across the country with your writer pals.

In addition to a stack of new content that's been added since launch (and more in this patch), we've also added the Author Outfits DLC to add some fresh styles to your fellow author companions. It's available right now for only $1.99, or even cheaper with the 25% launch discount until August 11.

Character Selector
Players who want to select which main character they'll play in Sometimes Always Monsters can now talk to the Dir. Nona character in the break room during the intro (while still controlling Shelly). There will be a conversation there that'll allow you to choose which player character you'd like to use.

Mobile DLC Control
We've added a new button to the phone that will allow players to control their DLC options remotely, rather than having to be on the bus. This means you can change any of the author outfits, or the party dogs at any point during the game.

After everything is said and done with the finale sequence, players will now have the option to join a fun party on the bus where they'll have an opportunity to read their (now preserved) novel to the other authors, hear their takes on your chapters, and talk a little about the journey you've shared before you all head back home.

There's a woman in Sequoia with a very old profession. Players can interact with her, and given a little covert language (and some funds) can spend the night off the bus having a little fun. Just pray that your spouse doesn't find out where you've been.

notes.title: Fans, Fury, & Puzzles - Build Update #447
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/24174678/f96e86b130b4e1e51b9aa20d454cddc5e61a74ee.png
Wow, this one took way longer than expected. That's the way it goes sometimes, apparently. For a single piece of content, the new fan (Aaron) turned out to require a significant amount of extra testing (Thanks Ash) because of it's many extra choices and endings.

It's one of those situations where we had this specific apex moment we wanted to reach, but the lead-to and fallout both required a sizable amount of variance to follow the "real choice" logic that SAM typically demands. Would have felt dishonest cutting the options short or pasting them into eachother, so it came down to just writing a ton of extra script and adding appropriate variability mechanics based on your character's stats. Anyway, it's a cool scene, and we hope you enjoy it.

Going forward, we hope to add more content like it if people are interested in it. It's a little less like some of the world-features, and a lot more story-focused. Though it's relatively isolated, it speaks to where the player is in terms of the main arc, at the point it happens. Let us know what you think of it.

New Fan: Aaron
In the latter days of your New Creole stop, players who explore the city may encounter a new NPC named Aaron. This character is a little disgruntled, a little opinionated, and a little aggressive about the new book that you're working on. He comes from a place of earnest passion, but things can quickly take a turn for the worse if he isn't satisfied by your answers during the confrontation. There are a lot of different ways that this encounter can end, but it's a fairly isolated incident. Be cautious, things can get ugly.

Spoilers: [spoiler]Fit players, and those who learned boxing in ASM will have an advantage here.[/spoiler]

Missing Puzzle Pieces
Not a terribly deep feature, but the authors on board the bus will now sometimes work on a puzzle that will complete itself over the course of the tour. There's a minor thread about a missing piece that needs the player's help, but it's a pretty dumb piece of content all-considered. More importantly it sets up a bit of framework that'll help expand future activities for authors sitting in the table-seats.

We had a really interesting weekend with LudoNarraCon and our first experiences doing development livestreams. It was really invigorating to have a bunch of you watch our process making new content, and join the chat to leave extra suggestions. We'd never considered having such a collaborative development experience, but it's been a lot of fun.

In addition to getting to talk with all of you and show off our ridiculous workflow, we actually got a lot of things finished. This update, more than others, has a lot of new content to enjoy. Check it all out:

New Content:
Seafood Vendors
Two new detailed NPCs are ready to sell you some fresh seafood, and can be found in New Creole and Gator Bay. They both deliver regional specialties, and offer players the opportunity to haggle prices on their daily catch. Just be sure to get to them in the morning, as stock dwindles over the day and costs go up before they completely run out in the evening. Bring a friend with you to the buy and get a pinch of insight into how they feel about crustaceans.

New Store (Beef Heaven)
Where the old QuickStarter shop once stood in Sequoia, now hosts a new butchery called Beef Heaven. In there you can pick up some steaks for grilling, or meatballs for spaghetti. There's also veal and ground product, along with an exclusive new barbecue sauce. There's also a lot of little interactives, some new interactions with the authors, and some deep lore about Sequoia's farming industries. Plus, a subtle little nightmare for certain save importers.

Burgers w/ Friends Includes new achievement
Tired of eating food on the bus? Tired of eating alone? Grab your spouse, or one of the authors and head to Bullet Burger for a serious chow session. After buying your burgers, grab a seat with them and eat until the two of you can't stomach any more. Light conversations revealing more about the author's opinions of one another will come to light, and you'll be able to stake a claim about your friendships as well. Note that this is a one-time venture per friend, as few can stomach multiple monstrous burger chow sessions.

Never Have I Ever... Includes new achievement
Being stuck on a bus without much to do can lead to some pretty desperate plots for entertainment. Now, on evenings while rolling between cities, the authors have a chance of sparking up a game of "Never Have I Ever". During the game, the authors, the player, and their spouse will stand around, revealing truths about themselves while getting plastered. It's a good way of getting to know each other a little better, and to pass the time while you travel between towns.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/24174678/6e8e98ce623351beef24d37719ec4f9885aef8ab.pngOne of the most misunderstood things about ASM's conclusion was its alley finale. The sequences that bookend the start and end of the game. They're contentious in context with the rest of the story and a lot of people (self-included) find them at odds with the grander theme and message of the game. It's also caused some greater confusion for people importing their saves, assuming that characters ought be dead when they aren't.

All along, the alley finale was intended to be the furthest point in the SAM/ASM timeline. However, while it was powerful at the time, it was a bit poorly conceived in terms of its lasting effect on the total continuity. It became a creative handicap, and stopped serving real purpose partway through SAM's development. We had hoped more players would recognize it as a meta scene (it was never intended to affect the status of imports), but that was never explained well enough outside of forums and private discussions.

So, in our infinite power as creators, we are officially hand-waving that piece away as a dream. It's not an easy decision to make, considering how many people felt deeply about the sequence, but it is quite necessary to free SAM from those shackles, and let it grow. There is now a new sequence that runs at the start of the game when you import a save that explains it as such, and we're going to stick with that.
